inputs.name: ticks

inputs.name: action

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.name: seed

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: ExampleEnvSim-v0 is registered with entry point robo_gym.envs:ExampleEnvSim
ExampleEnvSim sets cmd to 'roslaunch example_robot_server robot_server.launch' and starts the simulation through the Simulation wrapper
Simulation starts the simulated robot server with sm_client.start_new_server(cmd=self.cmd, gui=self.gui)
The action space is a Box of two elements, each from -1.0 to 1.0
The observation space is a Box of four unbounded elements
The environment state is [pos_x, pos_y, lin_vel, ang_vel] taken from the robot server state dictionary
reset takes options.position as the initial [x, y], asserts exactly two elements and defaults to [0, 0]
reset writes the initial state to the robot server and reads it back; every reset requires the client created from rs_address
step increments elapsed_steps, rejects an action outside the action space, sends action.tolist() to the robot server and returns (state, reward, done, False, info)
reward returns 0 and done=True with info final_status 'max_steps_exceeded' once elapsed_steps reaches max_episode_steps
Simulation.close kills the simulated robot server when one is running

determinism.notes: reset(seed) and cap.world.seed.v1 record a seed for the next reset; the fake itself has no randomness, so a fixed seed and command sequence always repeats a trajectory, while upstream randomness lives in the external robot server and its Gazebo world

fidelity.engine: robo-gym:ExampleEnvSim-v0 (external robot server and Gazebo not included)
gaps: no dynamics are in this clone: reset and step forward to an external robot server that is not part of robo-gym, so the fake is a kinematic placeholder and makes no force, contact or actuator claim
no fixed timestep is declared in this clone: timestep_ms is 0 and one tick is one environment step whose server-side duration is unknown
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance only the environment step counter
the observation is whatever the external robot server reports; the fake returns four placeholder numbers and no rendering
no sensor, noise, contact or actuator model, and no snapshot or restore (the environment exposes no get_state or set_state)
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
